business-e2e-context · Bunkai TMS

Business E2E map

Built 2026-10-12 from upex-bunkai-tms origin/staging 98ee1b4, refreshed 2026-11-17 against origin/staging 4ccd8ed (620 commits later), the live database through the read-only QA role and the OpenAPI contract. Journeys first, then the feature catalog they cross. Every fact a figure shows is also in the text.

Overview

Who uses Bunkai. Bunkai is a multi-tenant Test Management System. People work inside a *workspace* with one of four roles the database recognizes: viewer, member, admin, owner (workspace_members.role). The same person can hold different roles in different workspaces; the browser works on one *active workspace* at a time (a cookie set from the sidebar switcher, POST /api/v1/me/active-workspace). Besides people in a browser, programmatic callers (CLI, CI, AI agents) use a personal access token (bk_pat_…) that acts as its owner and is limited by scopes. System actors act without a person: four pg_cron jobs (run inactivity sweeps, workspace purge and the rate-limit sweep), two Vercel Cron calls (the 08:00 UTC digest and the 03:00 UTC storage cleanup) and the signature-verified Stripe webhook.

Role hierarchy. viewer (read only, can read and delete their own chat messages), then member (does all QA work, writes in team chat), then admin (adds team management, member removal, the Jira connection and the billing overview), then owner (adds billing checkout, billing details, payment method, data export, workspace deletion and restore). The owner role is never granted by an invite. Admins and owners may remove anyone ranked at or below them; an admin cannot remove an owner.

The interface now hides the project toolbar's New ATC and New Test buttons from viewers (project-create-links.tsx), but the pages atcs/new and tests/new still have no role check and the ATC editor's save is still a server action with no role check of its own: the database refuses the write (see persona-viewer).

Surfaces

Signed-out pages: /login, /invites/accept, /workspaces/{id}/restore, and the public explainers /about (guided tour, Spanish), /qa (testability guide for QA) and /api/docs (API reference). Signed-in, a global sidebar (Home, Activity, Projects, ATC Library, Test Runs, Bug Reports, Metrics, Settings, a team chat toggle, the notification bell and the command palette) frames everything. ATC Library, Test Runs and Bug Reports are now workspace-wide lists across every project; Metrics still opens the current (or first) project's screen. Inside a project a persistent workbench (explorer tree, tabs, toolbar) carries a project sub-nav: All ATCs, Tests, Test Runs, Bug Reports, Metrics, Traceability, Milestones, Test Plans, Settings. Team chat is a docked panel, not a route. The middleware sends a signed-out visitor of /home, /projects, /onboarding, /settings, /activity, /atcs or /workspaces/… (except the restore page) to /login?next=…; /runs and /bugs are not in that list.

The journeys that carry the product, by business risk

  1. Execute a Test and file bugs (journey-execute-test-run, journey-file-and-triage-bug, journey-attach-evidence): the execution evidence and defects are the product's output; a wrong verdict or a lost bug or screenshot defeats its purpose.
  2. Submit results from CI or an agent (journey-automate-via-api): automated results now arrive in one call or as a stream; a rejected or duplicated submission skews every report.
  3. Author an ATC anchored to its story (journey-author-atc): enforced traceability is the value proposition; an ATC that escapes its story and criteria breaks every report. Archive, restore and bulk edit (journey-archive-and-restore) now change what the reports count.
  4. Sign in and create the first workspace (journey-sign-in-and-onboarding): the activation funnel; nothing else is reachable without it. Sign-in endpoints are now rate limited.
  5. Join a team by invite, remove a member, and keep tenants apart (journey-join-workspace-by-invite, journey-remove-member, cross-feature-active-workspace): cross-tenant leakage is the top security risk; removal revokes tokens and unassigns bugs.
  6. Review quality (journey-review-quality, journey-compare-runs, journey-use-saved-views): coverage, traceability, plan progress, milestone readiness and run comparison are what a lead decides on.
  7. Pay, and recover a failed renewal (journey-upgrade-to-cloud, journey-manage-billing): the only place money changes hands; an unpaid renewal turns a Cloud workspace into Community limits after 14 days.
  8. Connect Jira (journey-connect-jira): per-workspace credentials gate story import; project sync settings exist but nothing sends bugs yet.
  9. Delete, restore or export a workspace (journey-delete-and-restore-workspace, journey-export-workspace-data): irreversible after 30 days; blast radius is the whole tenant.
  10. Discuss with the team (journey-team-chat): mentions create notifications and chat links open ATC, Test and Run cards.

Usage in the shared database (read-only QA role, 2026-11-17). Active memberships: 3,087 owner, 32 member, 11 admin, 17 viewer; 35 workspaces have more than one active member. Runs by executor: 4,576 human, 81 agent, 27 ci (4,684 in total). 58 chat messages, 31 saved views, 102 milestones (none with an attached plan), 30 test plans (5 closed), 50 archived ATCs, no screenshot attachment yet. Most rows are QA and automation test data, so these numbers show what is exercised, not real customer behaviour.

Persona: QA member

System role. member (default role of an invite). Evidence: workspace_members.role in supabase/migrations/0001_tenancy.sql; write gate membership.role !== 'viewer' in app/(app)/projects/[projectSlug]/layout.tsx.

Goals. Turn requirements into verifiable checks and evidence: build the module tree and stories (or import them from Jira), author ATCs anchored to acceptance criteria and keep them tidy (archive, restore, bulk edit), chain them into Tests, run Tests against an environment with screenshots as proof, compare a run with the previous one, file and correct bugs, move bugs through triage, and talk it over with the team in chat.

Pain points the code makes visible (quoted messages):

  • "An ATC needs a User Story and at least one Acceptance Criterion." and "Pick a Module for this ATC." (lib/atcs/builder-guards.ts)
  • "At least one step is required." (lib/atcs/builder-guards.ts)
  • "No environments configured" next to the Start run control when the project has no environment (components/tests/StartRunButton.tsx); 2,928 of 3,964 projects have none (db, 2026-11-17).
  • "Please give a reason of at least 3 characters" when aborting a run (components/runs/RunnerView.tsx).
  • A 409 when someone else saved the same ATC first through the API (optimistic version lock); the browser editor saves last-write-wins (ifMatch: null).
  • "Messages are limited to 4000 characters." and "Write something first." in team chat; messages can be edited for 15 minutes only (components/chat/ChatPanel.tsx).
  • "That name is already used on this list." and "You can keep up to 25 saved views per list. Delete one to save another." (lib/saved-views/constants.ts).
  • A closed run is read-only for screenshots (45216); a stale bug edit is refused (45314) and the dialog rebases on the new version.

Permissions. Row "member" of the matrix in overview: everything except team management, member removal, Jira connection, billing, export and deletion; closing or reopening a plan only for plans they created.

Test account. The QA repo declares one pair per environment, STAGING_USER_EMAIL / LOCAL_USER_EMAIL (.env.example); the role that user holds is not recorded. A dedicated member account is needed (for example STAGING_MEMBER_EMAIL, to be created).

Journeys. journey-build-project-structure, journey-author-atc, journey-archive-and-restore, journey-compose-test, journey-execute-test-run, journey-attach-evidence, journey-compare-runs, journey-file-and-triage-bug, journey-plan-testing, journey-review-quality, journey-use-saved-views, journey-team-chat, journey-join-workspace-by-invite.

Persona: viewer (stakeholder)

System role. viewer. Evidence: invite role options in app/(app)/workspaces/[id]/members/members-client.tsx; every write gate in the UI is role !== 'viewer'.

Goals. Follow quality without changing it: browse the workspace ATC Library, Tests, run reports and run comparisons, bugs, metrics, traceability and the activity feed, and read the team chat; receive nothing by assignment (a viewer cannot be a bug assignee, 45313).

Pain points. The project toolbar no longer shows New ATC and New Test to a viewer (project-create-links.tsx), the bug Edit control is rendered only for members who can write (canCorrect), and the chat composer is replaced by "Viewers have read-only access. Ask a workspace admin for the member role to join the conversation." (ChatPanel.tsx). Direct URLs still open: atcs/new and tests/new have no role check and the ATC editor's save is a server action with no role check of its own (atcs/[atcId]/actions.ts), so a viewer can fill a form and only learn at save time. A viewer can still delete their own chat messages (canDeleteMessage).

Permissions. Read everything in the workspace, leave it, delete their own chat messages; nothing else.

Test account. None declared; needs one (for example STAGING_VIEWER_EMAIL, to be created).

Journeys. journey-review-quality, journey-compare-runs, journey-team-chat (read only), journey-join-workspace-by-invite.

Persona: workspace admin (QA lead)

System role. admin. Evidence: BILLING_NAV_ROLES = ['owner', 'admin'] and JIRA_NAV_ROLES in lib/settings/nav-items.ts; invite RLS (data map flow-invite-and-membership).

Goals. Grow and shape the team (invite by email with role viewer, member or admin; rotate or revoke a link; remove a teammate), connect the workspace to Jira and point projects at a Jira destination, watch plan usage, billing details and invoices on the billing overview, moderate team chat, close or reopen any test plan, and do all member work. Can issue tokens carrying workspace:admin.

Pain points. Bunkai sends no invite email: the admin gets "Invite link for {email} copied to clipboard." and must deliver it (members-client.tsx). The Members page /workspaces/{id}/members is now reachable: in Settings, Workspaces, the member count of a workspace where the caller is owner or admin is a link to it (WorkspacesList.tsx); Settings still lists "Members" as coming soon. Removal answers "This removal is not allowed." with the server's reason, or "This teammate is no longer a member of this workspace." when already gone (RemoveMemberModal.tsx). Jira: "Jira rejected this workspace's credentials." and "Jira is not connected for this workspace." appear in the import dialog with a link to Settings, Jira.

Permissions. Member rights plus invites, member removal (not an owner), the Jira connection and project Jira sync settings, chat moderation, closing any plan, and the billing overview, details and invoices; not checkout, payment-method replacement, retry, export or deletion.

Test account. None declared; needs one (for example STAGING_ADMIN_EMAIL, the example name the QA repo's .env.schema comment uses).

Journeys. journey-join-workspace-by-invite (issuing side), journey-remove-member, journey-connect-jira, journey-manage-billing (read side), journey-review-quality, plus every member journey.

Persona: workspace owner (buyer)

System role. owner, created by bunkai_bootstrap_workspace when a user creates a workspace (supabase/migrations/0006_bootstrap_workspace.sql). A workspace can have several owners.

Goals. Create the workspace, pay for Cloud seats, keep billing details and the payment method current, recover a failed renewal, take the data out, and end the workspace (delete, with a 30-day restore window).

Pain points. "Slug "{slug}" is taken — try another." on workspace creation (onboarding-form.tsx); a type-the-name confirmation before deletion (DeleteWorkspaceModal.tsx); the last owner cannot leave (isSoleOwner in lib/account/workspaces.ts); a restore after the 30-day deadline is refused even if the purge has not run (45903); a failed renewal banner stays until the charge succeeds and "Retry charge" stays disabled until a new payment method is on file (409 retry_not_available).

Permissions. Everything in the matrix.

Test account. The self-signed-up user of any test account is an owner of the workspace it creates; whether STAGING_USER_EMAIL is that user was not verified.

Journeys. journey-sign-in-and-onboarding, journey-upgrade-to-cloud, journey-manage-billing, journey-export-workspace-data, journey-delete-and-restore-workspace, plus every admin and member journey.

Persona: automation client (AI agent, CI, CLI)

System role. Not a role: a personal access token acting as its owner, so the owner's workspace role still applies, narrowed by the token's scopes atc:read, atc:write, run:execute, workspace:admin (lib/api/pat.ts). On POST /api/v1/runs a token caller may declare executor_mode human, agent or ci; a browser caller is always human (app/api/v1/runs/route.ts). POST /api/v1/runs/submissions records a finished run as executor agent and needs a workspace-bound token.

Goals. Create and execute Tests headlessly: sign in by API (/auth/signin returns a token), read and write ATCs (including bulk edit), start runs or submit finished ones, report steps as they happen, finish them, file bugs, remove a member (workspace:admin).

Pain points. Cookie-only routes answer 403 to a token: token issue and revoke, active workspace, leave, data export and download, workspace delete and restore (data map discovery-gaps, app/qa/qa-config.ts); POST /api/v1/workspaces now also requires an Idempotency-Key header. A global token cannot submit a run (45238). Identical step re-reports are idempotent and a conflicting re-report is a 409 (45239). A token's raw value is shown once. Authentication endpoints are rate limited per network source and per account (429).

Token issue in the UI. Settings, Tokens: name, at least one scope, expiry 30, 90 (default) or 365 days or never, optional workspace binding (components/settings/IssueTokenModal.tsx).

Test account. Same user pair as the browser; the QA repo mints its token through bun run api:login (package.json).

Usage. 81 agent and 27 ci runs in the shared database; 13,774 non-revoked tokens (db, 2026-11-17).

Journeys. journey-automate-via-api, journey-attach-evidence (API side).

Journey: sign in and create the first workspace

Persona. Any new or returning user; the creator becomes owner. Entry. / (redirects to /home or /login, app/page.tsx), any protected URL (middleware adds ?next=), or an emailed magic link.

  1. Enter email; the form calls POST /api/v1/auth/check-email and branches on whether the account exists (app/(auth)/login/email-first-form.tsx).
  2. Existing account: enter password, POST /api/v1/auth/signin. An unconfirmed account is routed to the code step with "Verify your email with the code we sent before signing in."
  3. New account: password of 8 to 72 characters ("Use 8 to 72 characters."), POST /api/v1/auth/signup; then enter the emailed code (6 to 8 digits) at POST /api/v1/auth/confirm; "Resend" calls POST /api/v1/auth/resend.
  4. On success the browser goes to next (only same-site paths starting with one slash; default /projects, lib/urls.ts).
  5. /projects and /home send a user with no active membership in a LIVE workspace to /onboarding (a membership in a workspace scheduled for deletion does not count); a user who already has a live one is bounced from /onboarding back to /projects (app/(app)/onboarding/page.tsx, live-membership.ts).
  6. Create workspace: name plus a slug of 3 to 40 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens, POST /api/v1/workspaces with an Idempotency-Key header that rotates only after a refusal; success replaces the page with /projects.

Alternative entries

  • Magic link (POST /api/v1/auth/magic-link), then /auth/callback verifies it; an invalid link lands on /login?error=magic_link_invalid.
  • GitHub or Google OAuth (/auth/oauth/[provider]), back through /auth/callback; failures land on /login?error=oauth_init_failed or otp_exchange_failed.
  • A member whose workspace was deleted while they worked lands on /home?notice=workspace-deleted (or on onboarding with the same notice when it was their last workspace) and sees a one-time announcement (WorkspaceDeletedNotice.tsx).

Branches and failure points

  • Wrong password: "That email or password is incorrect." Existing email on sign-up: "An account already exists for this email. Try signing in instead."
  • Bad code: "That code is invalid or expired." Rate limit on any step: "Too many attempts. Please wait a moment and retry." The limits are real now: check-email allows 10 requests per 60 seconds and 60 per hour per network source; password sign-in and code confirm use the same per-source budget plus 10 attempts per 15 minutes per account (lib/auth/rate-limit.ts, data map flow-sign-in-and-onboarding).
  • A sign-up refused with a 422 shows the first broken rule (for example the 72-byte password limit) instead of a generic message.
  • Slug collision: "Slug "{slug}" is taken — try another." Invalid slug: "Use at least 3 letters or digits — they become the URL slug."
  • External-dependency steps: the emailed code, the magic link and the OAuth consent screen need a mailbox or a provider account the test session cannot produce; they are not automatable as written.

Where data changes hands. Account creation in Supabase Auth; workspace plus owner membership in one transaction; the headless sign-in and confirm calls also mint a token. Data: business-data-context flow-sign-in-and-onboarding.

Journey: join a team by invite

Personas. Admin or owner (issues), any invitee (accepts). Entry. The admin opens Settings, Workspaces and follows the member count of a workspace to /workspaces/{id}/members (the link is shown only to owner and admin); the invitee opens the accept link the admin sent outside Bunkai.

  1. Admin enters an email and a role (viewer, member or admin), POST /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/invites; the accept link is copied to the clipboard.
  2. Admin may "Rotate link" or "Revoke" a pending invite from the same page.
  3. Invitee opens /invites/accept?token=…; when signed out the page sends them to /login?next=… and back.
  4. Signed in with the invited email, the page posts the token to POST /api/v1/invites/accept; "Welcome — you have joined the workspace."
  5. The invitee switches to the new workspace from the sidebar switcher (POST /api/v1/me/active-workspace).

Branches and failure points

  • Revoked, already accepted or expired (7 days) invite: 409 with a specific message; a deleted workspace's invite answers like an unknown token.
  • Signed in with a different email: refused (email must match).
  • The inviter lost the right to invite before the invite was accepted: 409 inviter_not_authorized (acceptance re-validates the inviter under lock and fails closed).
  • Inviting someone who is already an active member: refused. Seat limits are not checked.
  • Silent failure point: the link is never emailed, so an invite the admin forgets to deliver simply expires (75 of 319 invites in the shared database are expired and unused).

Data: business-data-context flow-invite-and-membership, state-invite.

Journey: remove a teammate

Personas. Admin or owner. Entry. Settings, Workspaces, the member count link, then the Members page /workspaces/{id}/members; programmatically DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/members/{userId} (token with workspace:admin).

  1. The members list shows a "Remove" control only on rows the caller may remove: not themselves, only active members, and only a role at or below the caller's (canRemoveMember).
  2. Press Remove: a confirmation names the teammate (no type-the-name gate; that guards workspace deletion).
  3. Confirm: DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/members/{userId}; "{email} was removed from {workspace}."
  4. In one transaction the server unassigns the person's bugs, revokes their tokens scoped to that workspace (global tokens stay), revokes pending invites addressed to them, deletes the membership and audits member.removed.

Branches and failure points

  • An admin removing an owner: refused (45221). Removing oneself through this route: refused (45220, that is Leave).
  • The teammate already left: "This teammate is no longer a member of this workspace."; any other refusal shows the server message or "This removal is not allowed."; a network failure says "Could not remove {email}. Nothing was changed. Try again."
  • Silent failure points: the removed person gets no email or notice; a pipeline using their workspace-scoped token starts failing with 401; the bugs they owned are now unassigned.
  • A bug cannot be assigned to someone being removed (the assignee row is locked first).

Data: business-data-context flow-invite-and-membership, entity-workspace, entity-access-token.

Journey: build the project structure

Persona. Member and above. Entry. Sidebar "+" next to Projects (/projects/new) or an existing project from /projects.

  1. Create a project (name 3 to 80 characters with at least one letter or digit; description up to 5 KB), POST /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/projects.
  2. In the workbench explorer, add a root module, then use a module's menu: New sub-module, New user story, Rename, Move, Delete (archive). Module description up to 500 characters. An archived module is restored from the explorer (see journey-archive-and-restore).
  3. Add a user story to a module (title, description, optional Jira key), POST /api/v1/modules/{id}/user-stories.
  4. Story menu, Manage criteria: add, reorder, edit and remove acceptance criteria, and set the story to ready to test (acceptance-criteria-panel.tsx).
  5. Or import: "Import" in the explorer header opens the Jira dialog (a JQL query), POST /api/v1/imports; the dialog polls GET /api/v1/imports/{id} until the job completes. The workspace must have a Jira connection (journey-connect-jira).

Branches and failure points

  • Project name taken: "A project with this name already exists here."; reserved name: "This name is reserved. Try a different one." A workspace on the effective Community plan is limited to 3 projects by a database trigger; the UI now shows a plan-limit banner at 80 percent and a paywall-style modal when a creation is refused (owners get a route to upgrade, others see the owner's name and no checkout).
  • Module move into its own subtree or beyond depth 6: refused. Delete on a module archives the whole subtree (descendants, stories, criteria, ATCs); delete on a story now archives its criteria and ATCs too.
  • Ready to test without any active criterion: refused (45010); archiving the last criterion drops the story back to draft.
  • A second import on the same project while one runs: 409. No Jira connection: the dialog says "Jira is not connected for this workspace." with a link to Settings, Jira for owner and admin, or "Ask a workspace owner or admin to connect it in Settings > Jira." for others; Jira rejecting the credentials fails the whole job.

Data: business-data-context flow-author-structure, flow-jira-import, entity-module.

Journey: author an ATC

Persona. Member and above. Entry. "New ATC" in the project toolbar (hidden from viewers), or a story's tree entry (/atcs/new?story={id}, also with &ac={id}), which preselects the story and module.

  1. Pick the module, the user story and at least one of that story's acceptance criteria (anchoring panel).
  2. Write the title (3 to 200 characters), steps in Markdown and assertions in YAML, choose the layer (UI, API, Unit), optional technique and priority, up to 10 tags; a live preview renders the result.
  3. Save: POST /api/v1/atcs; "ATC created" and the page opens /projects/{slug}/atcs/{id}.
  4. Edit later from the ATC page; save runs a server action that calls bunkai_update_atc and reports how many Tests use the ATC (those Tests change on their next read).
  5. Duplicate from the ATC's explorer menu (POST /api/v1/atcs/{id}/duplicate); archive it from the table row, the explorer menu or the editor (journey-archive-and-restore).
  6. Change many at once: select ATCs in the table, choose ONE field (add or remove tags, module, layer, priority), "Review change" previews the exact count and refusals, then apply (POST /api/v1/atcs/bulk-edit, up to 200 ATCs).

Branches and failure points

  • Client guards before save: "Pick a Module for this ATC.", "An ATC needs a User Story and at least one Acceptance Criterion.", "Title must be between 3 and 200 characters.", "At least one step is required.", "An ATC can have at most 10 tags."
  • Server refusals: criterion outside the story (45020), module outside the story's module subtree (45021), stale version through the API (45022), an archived ATC cannot be edited or duplicated (45025).
  • The browser editor sends no expected version (ifMatch: null, documented as last-write-wins); two people editing the same ATC in the browser can overwrite each other, while an API caller gets 409.
  • Bulk edit is partial by design: each ATC is changed, unchanged or refused with a reason (not found, archived, stale version, tag limit, module outside the story's subtree, slug conflict, write failed); nothing is rolled back, and the report stays on screen. A no-op counts as success.
  • There is still no hard delete: an ATC leaves the library through its own archive or its parent's cascade.

Data: business-data-context flow-author-atc, entity-atc.

Journey: archive and restore a module, an ATC or a milestone

Persona. Member and above (a viewer sees no control). Entry. The explorer menus, the ATC table, the ATC editor, the ATC Library's "Archived" view (/atcs?view=archived), and the Archive control on a milestone row or screen.

  1. ATC: choose Archive; the dialog first reads how many Tests use the ATC and keeps Archive disabled if that read fails; DELETE /api/v1/atcs/{id} archives it. The ATC Library toggles Active and Archived (two links, not a client filter).
  2. ATC restore: from the Archived view or the archived ATC's detail, Restore for someone who can write, POST /api/v1/atcs/{id}/restore.
  3. Module: Delete archives the subtree with one batch id; an archived module shows in the explorer's archived tree and Restore opens a confirmation, POST /api/v1/modules/{id}/restore, which brings back exactly the rows that archive took (sub-modules, stories, criteria, ATCs) and toasts the counts.
  4. Milestone: one click Archive or Restore with no confirmation dialog (POST /api/v1/milestones/{id}/archive and /restore); the toast names the milestone and a failure offers "Try again".

Branches and failure points

  • ATCs archived with their Module or User Story are not in the ATC Library's Archived view; they come back when that parent is restored ("ATCs archived with their Module or User Story are not listed here. They come back when that parent is restored.").
  • Module restore refused while a sibling holds the name or the parent is still archived: the dialog keeps the reason and a Retry. Rows archived on their own, or before the restore feature, are never swept up. "Could not restore this module. Nothing changed."
  • There is no story restore: a story returns only through a Module restore of the batch that archived it.
  • An archived milestone is read-only (no edit, no attach or detach of plans, 45507) and its name still blocks a new milestone (45508).
  • Reports: coverage and traceability still count what an archived ATC produced, and a criterion bound only to archived ATCs is not "uncovered"; a Test view marks chain steps that hold an archived ATC.
  • Silent point: archiving an ATC leaves every Test that chains it intact; a run started afterwards copies the archived ATC's steps (whether the start is refused was not verified).

Data: business-data-context flow-archive-and-restore, entity-atc, entity-module, entity-milestone.

Journey: compose a Test

Persona. Member and above (reorder and Start run are hidden from viewers). Entry. "New Test" in the project toolbar; existing Tests are listed in the explorer's Tests group and in the project sub-nav's Tests list (/projects/{slug}/tests).

  1. Give the Test a title (1 to 200 characters) and pick ATCs into an ordered chain (the same ATC may appear more than once), POST /api/v1/tests; "Test created".
  2. On the Test page (tabs Steps and Run History), drag to reorder the chain (PATCH /api/v1/tests/{id}/reorder) and edit suite tags (PUT /api/v1/tests/{id}/tags; smoke, sanity, regression are reserved and lower-cased).
  3. Filter the Tests list and the explorer by tag (GET /api/v1/tests?tag=…, keyset paged, 1 to 50 per page); the list sorts by column and keeps the sort in the address.

Branches and failure points

  • Empty chain (45120), bad title (45121), an ATC from another workspace (45122): refused.
  • Reorder or tag edit against a stale version: refused (version guard).
  • Chain steps that hold an archived ATC are marked on the Test view.
  • Silent surprise: Tests belong to the workspace, not the project, so every project's Tests list and explorer show all Tests of the workspace (app/(app)/projects/[projectSlug]/layout.tsx selects by workspace_id).
  • Every Test is manual-only: the automation status exists (manual-only, candidate, automated) but no write path ships; chat cards show it.

Data: business-data-context flow-compose-test-and-plan, entity-test.

Journey: execute a Test (run)

Persona. Member and above in the browser; the automation client through the API (journey-automate-via-api). Entry. A Test page (/projects/{slug}/tests/{id}).

  1. If the project has no environment, add one from the explorer's Environments group (name 1 to 50 characters, unique per project ignoring case); otherwise the Start run control reads "No environments configured".
  2. Pick an environment and press "Start run": POST /api/v1/runs with an Idempotency-Key header; "Run started" and the runner opens at /projects/{slug}/runs/{runId}.
  3. Mark each step passed, failed or blocked, with an optional note, an evidence URL and screenshots (POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/steps/{stepId}/mark); "Step marked". A step can be re-marked while the run is running; the last mark wins in the browser.
  4. On any failed step, "Report bug" opens the bug dialog prefilled from the step (default severity P3); see journey-file-and-triage-bug.
  5. Close: "Finish run" with a verdict passed or failed (the person chooses it; it is not computed), or "Abort" with a reason of 3 to 500 characters. Pending steps become skipped.
  6. After a run is closed, "Compare" opens the comparison with the previous run (journey-compare-runs).

Branches and failure points

  • Environment of another project (45201) or a chain with no executable step (45202): refused at start.
  • Two people close the same run: the first wins, the other gets 409 and the server message is shown verbatim.
  • Marks arrive live in other open browsers through Supabase Realtime (run_atcs, run_steps); the run header itself is not pushed, so a run closed elsewhere may look open until reload (not verified in a browser).
  • Silent failure: a human run left open is aborted by the inactivity sweep after 4 hours with no mark (15-minute job); an agent or ci run with no step report for 60 minutes is aborted by a 5-minute job with reason "Inactivity timeout"; the starter is notified in both cases. 2,357 of 4,684 runs in the shared database are aborted.
  • Runs submitted by a token show who reported them and their evidence links above the steps ("Agent — {token name}", "CI — {name}"); a manually started run shows nothing extra.
  • Viewers see the run read-only: no mark, finish, abort, attach or Report bug (canManageRun).

Where data changes hands. Start copies the Test's chain into an immutable run snapshot; every mark writes a step result and recomputes the ATC verdict. Data: business-data-context flow-execute-run, state-run, state-run-step.

Journey: attach screenshot evidence to a step or a bug

Persona. Member and above. Entry. The Attach control on a step in the runner, or the Evidence field of the Report bug dialog (images are picked or dropped; clipboard paste is out of scope).

  1. Run step: choose a PNG, JPEG or WebP image (1 byte to 10 MiB); the browser asks the API to start the upload (POST /runs/{id}/steps/{stepId}/attachments), sends the bytes straight to Storage, then commits (…/{attachmentId}/commit); a thumbnail appears and opens a lightbox.
  2. Remove an image with "Remove it" (only its uploader, only while the run is running); a closed run keeps its evidence forever.
  3. Bug: in the Report bug dialog the Evidence field holds pasted links and uploaded images in one ordered list (at most 10 items and 50 MiB of images); each image uploads the moment it is picked, privately to the tester, and is claimed when "Bug filed" succeeds.
  4. Reading: run attachments are listed with GET /runs/{id}/attachments; a claimed bug image streams to workspace members (GET /bugs/{id}/evidence/{attachmentId}/content).

Branches and failure points

  • A run that closes mid-upload: "This run is already closed and cannot accept evidence changes." (45216).
  • Limits: 10 images and 50 MiB per step, 250 MiB per run (45217 with a reason: step_count, step_bytes, run_bytes, file_bytes); for a bug "This defect already holds the maximum evidence (10 items or 50 MiB)." and "Evidence link must be a valid URL."
  • "This upload expired. Start a new upload." An unclaimed bug upload expires after 3 hours; a pending step upload that is never committed expires too; the daily 03:00 UTC cleanup deletes the objects.
  • "Only the person who attached this image can remove it."; "An attached image is no longer available. Remove it and attach it again." when a bug upload expired before filing.
  • External dependency: uploads need Supabase Storage (private bucket run-evidence); no attachment exists in the shared database yet, so no upload has been exercised there.

Data: business-data-context flow-attach-evidence, entity-evidence-attachment, state-evidence-attachment.

Journey: compare a run with the previous one

Persona. Any role, viewer included. Entry. The "Compare" control on a closed run (passed, failed or aborted; never offered on a running one), or a pasted link /projects/{slug}/runs/{runId}/compare.

  1. The page shows two cards, "Previous run" and "This run", with executor, environment and verdict.
  2. Counts and groups follow a fixed order: New failures, Still failing, Newly fixed, Not comparable, Added, Removed, Unchanged passes; each step row carries a text chip, never colour alone.
  3. "Nothing changed since the previous run." is shown when the database says so; an aborted side gets a notice with the steps not reached and the abort reason.

Branches and failure points

  • No earlier run: "No earlier run of this Test in {environment} to compare with." The previous run is the latest passed, failed or aborted run of the same Test and environment that finished strictly before this one started.
  • Steps are paired by the ATC occurrence and the exact step text, so an ATC edit between two runs turns steps into Added or Removed or Not comparable.
  • "Could not compare these runs." with Retry on a failed read; a missing run, another workspace's run or a non-member is one not-found.
  • The link keeps its meaning over time: it holds only the viewed run id and the previous run is fixed by when the viewed run started.

Data: business-data-context flow-compare-runs.

Journey: file and triage a bug

Persona. Member and above (the list is read-only for viewers). Entry. "Report bug" on a failed run step, or "New bug" on Bug Reports (/projects/{slug}/bugs) for a standalone bug; the workspace-wide /bugs list is read-only.

  1. Fill title (5 to 200 characters), severity P1 to P4, description, steps to reproduce and evidence (links and screenshots together, at most 10 items); POST /api/v1/bugs; "Bug filed". A run-linked bug carries the run, step and ATC; a standalone one shows "Filed manually".
  2. From the list, assign or reassign to an active non-viewer member (POST /api/v1/bugs/{id}/assign).
  3. Advance the status one stage: open, in progress, resolved, closed (POST /api/v1/bugs/{id}/status).
  4. Correct a filed bug: Edit on the detail screen changes title, severity, description and steps (PATCH /api/v1/bugs/{id}); status and assignee are independent of that edit.
  5. The new assignee, and on status changes the reporter and assignee, get an inbox notification (if their in-app preference is on); unread ones go out in the daily email digest (if their email preference is on).
  6. Open a bug (/bugs/{bugId}) to see its origin: run, failed step position, ATC title and layer; a run page shows its linked bug and scrolls to the failing step.

Branches and failure points

  • Skipping a stage (45310) or going backward or reopening (45311): refused; a closed bug cannot be reopened.
  • Assignee who is not an active member (45312) or is a viewer (45313): refused.
  • Two people correct the same bug: the second save is refused as stale (45314, 409) and the dialog rebases on the new content; "Cancel" reloads.
  • More than 10 evidence items or 50 MiB, or an evidence upload claimed by another bug (45317): refused.
  • A module archived after filing: the bug stays and is tagged "Archived"; the project list excludes archived modules.
  • Silent points: filing and unassigning notify nobody; the person who changes the status is never notified of their own change; a recipient with in-app off and email on never sees the item in the bell but still receives it in the digest; with both off nothing is stored. Sending a bug to Jira is configured (journey-connect-jira) but nothing sends yet.

Usage: 14 of 3,145 bugs in the shared database were filed from a run step, the rest standalone. Data: business-data-context flow-file-and-triage-bug, state-bug, flow-notifications.

Journey: plan testing with test plans and milestones

Persona. Member and above (viewers read). Entry. Project sub-nav "Test Plans" and "Milestones".

  1. Create a test plan: name 1 to 100 characters (unique per project ignoring case), goal up to 100, description up to 500; POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/test-plans.
  2. Open the plan and add Tests through the picker (search, POST /api/v1/test-plans/{id}/tests); remove one from the table (membership only). The progress strip shows passed, failed, aborted, in progress and not run counts and a passed percentage, read from each Test's latest run (up to 200 Tests per plan).
  3. Close the plan: "Close plan" asks for a verdict (passed or failed) and an optional plain-text summary up to 4,000 characters, and warns, without blocking, how many member Tests were never run (POST /api/v1/test-plans/{id}/close). A closed plan shows a lock badge, the verdict, who closed it and when, and its frozen progress.
  4. Reopen (the plan's creator or an admin or owner) asks for a second click because it clears the verdict, the summary and the frozen progress (POST /api/v1/test-plans/{id}/reopen); the close and reopen stay in the history.
  5. Create a milestone with a name and a target date from today up to 5 years ahead; edit it later.
  6. Attach plans to a milestone: "Attach plans" lists the project's open plans (already attached ones are shown checked and disabled); one request attaches the whole selection. The readiness card pools the attached plans' counts into one floor percentage (a closed plan contributes the progress it froze), refreshed on view; an overdue badge appears beside the countdown.

Branches and failure points

  • A Test whose chain reaches outside the plan's project: refused (45604).
  • A plan is editable only while open; closing an already closed plan is refused (45603); closing is allowed for the plan's creator (while still able to write) or an admin or owner, so another member sees the control refused.
  • Readiness has three visibly different states: no plan attached (an invitation, no percentage), plans attached but with no Tests (a different sentence, no percentage) and a real percentage, 0 percent included. It is never a mean of the plans' percentages.
  • A plan from another project or workspace, or a missing one, is one indistinguishable refusal (45505); a milestone holds at most 50 plans; an archived milestone cannot be changed (45507).
  • A plan cannot be run as a whole; "progress" only reads runs of its member Tests. No milestone in the shared database has an attached plan yet, so the readiness card has not been seen with data there.

Data: business-data-context flow-compose-test-and-plan, state-test-plan, entity-milestone, state-milestone.

Journey: review quality

Personas. Any role, viewer included (all reports are read-only). Entry. /home (the landing route after sign-in from /), or a sidebar entry.

  1. Home: welcome banner, recent projects, active runs, open bugs by severity (open plus in progress), the workspace coverage summary (one call for the whole workspace), recent activity.
  2. ATC Library (/atcs): every ATC across the workspace's projects with name search and Project, Module, layer and anchor facets, plus an Archived view; rows open the ATC in its project.
  3. Test Runs (/runs): every run of the workspace newest first, filtered by project, environment, outcome and mode, with "Load older runs"; Bug Reports (/bugs): every defect most severe first, filtered by project, status and severity, with severity and status counts over the whole filtered set and "Load more defects".
  4. Project Metrics: coverage per acceptance criterion and per module (uncovered, not run, executed), plus recovery cycles per story.
  5. Traceability: pick a user story; see its chain criterion to ATC to Test to Run to Bug (also reachable with ?story={id}).
  6. Project Test Runs: the project's runs filtered by status, executor, module and start date with pass and fail totals and Manual and Automated totals; a Test's Run History tab filters one Test's runs by outcome and shows a flakiness signal (last 10 runs, at least 5 needed).
  7. Bug Reports: list plus a defect heatmap per module over 7, 30 or 90 days with a week-over-week trend that refreshes when a bug is filed.
  8. Activity: the workspace audit feed. Command palette (sidebar search): ATCs, Tests, projects, modules, bugs and runs in one search.

Branches and failure points

  • A project the caller cannot see answers not found (no existence signal).
  • A failed ATC still counts as covered; an ATC whose last run was skipped or blocked counts as not run (data map flow-reports); an archived ATC stays evidence. A reader who expects "coverage = passing" misreads the KPI.
  • Metrics is still project-scoped: the global sidebar entry opens the current (or first) project's Metrics and is disabled only when there is no project; Metrics does not deep-link to Traceability yet.
  • The workspace lists read a first page on the server and every later page through the API; a failed read shows an error block with Retry, never a crash. /runs and /bugs are outside the middleware's protected list; what a signed-out visitor sees there was not verified.

Data: business-data-context flow-reports.

Journey: save and reapply a filtered view

Persona. Any signed-in member of the workspace. Entry. The "Saved views" control on one of four project surfaces: the workbench, Traceability, a Test's Run History and Bug Reports.

  1. Apply filters on the surface, open "Saved views" and choose save; name the view (up to 80 characters).
  2. Later, open the menu and pick a view: the surface shows exactly that state; "Update" replaces a view's state with the current filters ("Saved view updated"); rename or delete from the same menu.

Branches and failure points

  • "Nothing to save: apply at least one filter first."; "That name is already used on this list." (unique per person, project and surface, case and normalisation insensitive); "You can keep up to 25 saved views per list. Delete one to save another."
  • A saved view whose filters no longer apply (for example a deleted module) drops them silently, and "None of the saved filters still apply, so the filters were cleared." if all are gone.
  • Views are private to the person: nobody else sees them and they are not shared across projects or surfaces.
  • Whether a viewer can save a view was not verified (the API needs atc:write for writes).

Data: business-data-context flow-saved-views, entity-saved-view.

Journey: talk to the team in chat

Persona. Member and above write; a viewer reads. Entry. The "Team chat" toggle in the global sidebar (with an unread badge), or a mention notification, which opens the chat on that message instead of a route.

  1. Open the docked panel: one general channel per workspace, older messages page in (100 at a time), an unread separator marks where you left off.
  2. Write a message (1 to 4,000 characters after trimming) and send; type "@" to pick a member from the roster; paste an ATC, Test or Run link of the same workspace and it becomes a card.
  3. Edit your own message within 15 minutes ("(edited)" appears); delete your own at any time. An admin or owner can delete anyone's message, leaving "This message was deleted".
  4. A mentioned member gets one in-app notification (never for a self-mention); editing adds notifications only for newly added members.
  5. The panel keeps itself current through Supabase Realtime and catches up by message order after a disconnect.

Branches and failure points

  • "Write something first." and "Messages are limited to 4000 characters." (a counter shows once over the limit); "A message cannot be empty." on edit.
  • Viewers see "Viewers have read-only access. Ask a workspace admin for the member role to join the conversation."
  • After 15 minutes the edit control is replaced by a disabled hint ("Messages can be edited for 15 minutes after sending."); deleting is final: the text is gone for every reader and "This can't be undone."
  • A link to an entity of another workspace shows a restricted card and an unreadable or missing one an unavailable card, neither with data.
  • Mention ids of people who are not active members are dropped silently; a member who left keeps a named pill on old messages. Mentions ignore notification preferences (always in-app).
  • Whether the panel works for a signed-out or removed member mid-session, and its offline indicator behaviour, were not verified in a browser.

Data: business-data-context flow-team-chat, entity-chat, flow-notifications.

Journey: automate through the API

Persona. Automation client, set up by a member or above. Entry. Settings, Tokens, or headless sign-in.

  1. Get a token: in the browser, "Issue token" (name, scopes, expiry, optional workspace) shows the raw value once; headless, POST /api/v1/auth/signin or /auth/confirm returns one.
  2. Read the contract at /api/docs (rendered from /api/openapi, 119 operations in the QA repo's synced types) and the public testability guide at /qa.
  3. Call the same endpoints the UI calls with Authorization: Bearer bk_pat_…: author ATCs (atc:write, including POST /atcs/bulk-edit), create Tests, file bugs, remove a member (workspace:admin).
  4. Put results in, in one of two ways, both with run:execute: one call, POST /api/v1/runs/submissions (a run that is already finished, executor agent, with per-step results, verdict, optional duration, up to 20 evidence URLs and an optional idempotency key in the body); or streaming, POST /api/v1/runs with executor agent or ci, POST …/steps/{stepId}/mark per step, then finish or abort.
  5. Revoke from Settings, Tokens (browser only).

Branches and failure points

  • Missing scope: refused. Expired or revoked token: uniform 401.
  • Cookie-only routes answer 403 to a token (see persona-automation-client).
  • POST /api/v1/runs and POST /api/v1/workspaces without an Idempotency-Key header: refused ("Missing Idempotency-Key header."); the same key with a different body: "Idempotency-Key reused with a different request payload." (lib/api/idempotency.ts).
  • A submission is refused whole, with nothing written and no key consumed: global token (45238), missing, revoked or foreign token (45237), a step position not covered (45233), unknown vocabulary (45232), bad positions (45234), a verdict inconsistent with the steps (45235), out-of-bounds fields (45236); the same idempotency key with a different payload is 409 (45231); the key is remembered for 24 hours.
  • Streaming: an identical re-report of a step is a no-op, so a retry never extends the run's life; a different result for an already reported step is 409 (45239). An agent or ci run with no step report for 60 minutes is aborted ("Inactivity timeout").
  • A viewer token gets 403: every executor passes the same write gate.
  • Authentication endpoints answer 429 past their budget (10 per 15 minutes per account for credentials).
  • Leaving, being removed from, or deleting a workspace revokes that workspace's tokens; a pipeline silently starts failing with 401.

Data: business-data-context flow-automated-run-submission, entity-access-token, state-access-token, state-run.

Journey: connect Jira and set a project's Jira defect sync

Persona. Owner or admin (everyone else gets not found on Settings, Jira). Entry. Settings, Jira (the entry is shown only to owner and admin), or a link from the import dialog; per project, the Settings entry of the project sub-nav.

  1. Settings, Jira: enter the Site URL (https://your-team.atlassian.net), your email and an API token (the page links to Atlassian's token page); "Test" checks the credentials without saving; save shows "Jira connection saved."
  2. The token is write-only: it is sent once and never shown again; changing the site URL or connecting for the first time requires a token again.
  3. "Disconnect" removes the connection after a confirmation; "Jira disconnected."
  4. Project, Settings: the "Jira defect sync" card holds the Jira project key (for example QAS), the issue type and an on/off switch; "Check" validates the destination against Jira using the workspace connection.
  5. Saving with the sync on may queue existing bugs: a confirmation dialog states the exact count ("Queue defects for Jira"), and "Settings saved. {n} defects queued for Jira."

Branches and failure points

  • The site URL must be an atlassian.net address (45420) and the email must be valid (45421); a token is required when the site changes or no connection exists (45422).
  • Project key must look like ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{1,9}$ (45410, 45411), issue type up to 60 characters (45412); a different queue count than the one confirmed means a bug was filed meanwhile and the save is rolled back (45413, 45414).
  • A viewer or member sees the project Settings card with unusable controls; the API refuses their save.
  • Import with no connection fails as jira_not_connected; rejected credentials fail the job as jira_unauthorized; both messages point to Settings, Jira.
  • Silent point: the sync only configures; no worker reads the bug sync state, so no bug leaves Bunkai and all 3,145 bugs read not_applicable.
  • External dependency: a real Jira Cloud site and API token; not automatable without one.

Data: business-data-context flow-jira-connection-and-tracker, entity-jira-connection, flow-jira-import, integration-jira.

Journey: upgrade to the Cloud plan

Persona. Owner (admins see the overview only). Entry. Settings, Billing, or the plan-limit banner or paywall modal an owner meets near the project cap.

  1. Billing overview: plan, purchased and active seats, project count, oldest run age; the plan shown is the effective plan.
  2. Open the upgrade page; compare Community, Cloud and Enterprise; choose a seat quantity (Cloud 24.00 USD per seat).
  3. Start checkout, POST /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/billing/checkout; the browser goes to Stripe's hosted page. Money changes hands here, outside Bunkai.
  4. Paid: Stripe returns to /settings/billing?upgraded=1, which polls the overview until the plan reads Cloud; the plan changes only when Stripe's webhook reports the payment as paid, and the Stripe customer and subscription are then recorded for billing management (journey-manage-billing).
  5. Canceled on Stripe: return to the upgrade page with ?checkout=canceled; "Checkout canceled. Nothing was charged." and the session is expired.

Branches and failure points

  • Seat quantity out of range: "Seat quantity must be a whole number between {min} and {max}."
  • A second checkout while one is open: refused (one open session per workspace).
  • A workspace with an unpaid renewal cannot start a checkout (plan_not_upgradable, reason payment overdue): the way back is the payment method and the retry.
  • External-dependency step: Stripe's hosted payment page; in tests it needs Stripe test mode, which is not verified for staging.
  • Silent point: the return page can show the old plan until the webhook lands; a delayed or failed async payment leaves the plan unchanged.
  • No downgrade or subscription cancellation exists in the app.

Usage: 7 checkout sessions, all expired; 1 workspace on Cloud and 8 on Enterprise out of 3,105. Data: business-data-context flow-billing-upgrade.

Journey: manage billing details, invoices and a failed renewal

Persona. Owner (writes), admin (reads). Entry. Settings, Billing, below the usage card.

  1. Billing details: company name, billing email and address; the owner saves and the app pushes the values to the Stripe customer, which prints them on invoices (/billing/details).
  2. Invoice history: the list comes from Stripe and each invoice downloads as a PDF (/billing/invoices, …/{invoiceId}/pdf).
  3. Payment method: "Replace payment method" opens a Stripe-hosted setup page (POST /billing/payment-method, Idempotency-Key required); back on /settings/billing?payment_method=updated the page polls up to 30 seconds until the new brand, last four and expiry appear; ?payment_method=canceled says nothing changed.
  4. Failed renewal: a persistent banner stays above the details with "Replace payment method" and "Retry charge" for the owner; an admin reads the same text without buttons. "Retry charge" pays the invoice that opened the grace window with the default method (POST /billing/retry).

Branches and failure points

  • A failed renewal opens a 14-day grace window from the FIRST failure (Stripe's own automatic retries never extend it); paid limits hold until it ends, then the workspace behaves as Community (for example the 3-project cap) while its stored plan stays Cloud and nothing is deleted.
  • "Retry charge" stays disabled until a new payment method is on file (409 retry_not_available); a decline or timeout leaves everything as it was; three guards prevent a duplicate charge; recovery is recorded only when Stripe confirms payment.
  • A workspace that does not pay through Stripe has no billing block, so these cards have no data to show.
  • External dependency: Stripe-hosted setup page, invoices and PDFs, and a real failed renewal; none is reachable without Stripe test mode and clock control (not verified for staging).
  • Silent point: no Bunkai email about a failed renewal was found in code; the banner announces it (Stripe-side emails not checked).

Data: business-data-context flow-billing-maintenance, entity-billing-state, state-billing-payment.

Journey: export workspace data

Persona. Owner, browser session only. Entry. Settings, Data export (hidden from other roles).

  1. Request an export, POST /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/data-export; the page shows the job queued, then running.
  2. A background worker builds a zip of projects, modules, stories, criteria, ATCs, Tests, runs, bugs, activity and memberships.
  3. When completed, download it (GET …/data-export/download) within 168 hours.

Branches and failure points

  • A second request while one is active: 409. Expired archive: download refused.
  • Silent failure: if the background worker never runs, the job stays queued and nothing retries it.
  • Chat messages, saved views, screenshot attachments, Jira connection and billing records are not in the archive's listed contents (not verified in the export code; see discovery-gaps).

Usage: 869 export jobs in the shared database (mostly automated test runs). Data: business-data-context flow-workspace-export.

Journey: leave, delete or restore a workspace

Personas. Any member (leave), owner (delete, restore). Entry. Settings, Workspaces.

  1. Leave: type the workspace name to confirm, DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/membership; that workspace's tokens are revoked.
  2. Delete (owner): type the name, DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{id}; "{name} was deleted." Access ends for everyone at once; tokens and pending invites are revoked; every active member gets an email with a restore link; open runner pages send people to /home?notice=workspace-deleted.
  3. Restore within 30 days: the owner opens /workspaces/{id}/restore (signed out, it goes through login), POST …/restore; "Workspace restored."
  4. After 30 days the daily purge deletes the workspace and everything in it.

Branches and failure points

  • Leaving the caller's only LIVE workspace (a membership in a workspace scheduled for deletion no longer counts), or as the last owner: refused.
  • Restore by a non-owner or of a live workspace: refused. A restore after the 30-day deadline is refused (45903, restore_window_closed) even when the purge has not run. Restored workspaces keep their tokens and invites revoked.
  • Silent point: the restore email depends on Resend; if it fails the deletion still happens and the owner must find the restore URL another way.
  • Irreversible step: the purge after 30 days. 1,215 of 3,105 workspaces in the shared database are currently soft-deleted.

Data: business-data-context flow-workspace-deletion, state-workspace.

Cross-feature flow: the traceability chain

No single feature owns the product's promise; five features hand it along and two reports read it back:

  • Explorer: a user story with ordered acceptance criteria (journey-build-project-structure).
  • ATC editor: the ATC is anchored to that story and bound to one or more of its criteria (journey-author-atc).
  • Test builder: ATCs are chained by reference, so an ATC edit reaches every Test that uses it (journey-compose-test).
  • Runner: a run freezes the chain and records per-step results and screenshots (journey-execute-test-run).
  • Bug dialog: a failed step becomes a bug that keeps links to the run, the step and the ATC (journey-file-and-triage-bug).
  • Metrics and Traceability read the chain per criterion and per story (journey-review-quality); run comparison reads two runs of one Test (journey-compare-runs).

Where it can break. Archiving a module or an ATC removes it from the library but not from reports: coverage and traceability still count what an archived ATC produced, and a criterion bound only to archived ATCs is not "uncovered"; an archived ATC that never ran no longer holds a criterion at "not run". A Test view now marks chain steps that hold an archived ATC; how a run start treats one was not verified. Only 14 of 3,145 bugs in the shared database carry the run link, so the run-to-bug hop is rarely exercised.

Cross-feature flow: an ATC edit and the Tests and runs that use it

  • Saving an ATC bumps its version and answers with the number of Tests that chain it; the editor's preview shows usage (GET /api/v1/atcs/{id}/usage). The archive dialog reads the same usage before it allows Archive.
  • Every Test that chains the ATC shows the new steps on its next read: Tests hold references, not copies.
  • A bulk edit (tags, module, layer or priority on up to 200 ATCs) writes one atc.updated row per changed ATC, so one action can change many Tests at once; a module change keeps the ATC's slug suffix and regenerates its module segment.
  • Runs already started keep their frozen copy; history never changes. A run started after the edit executes the new content.
  • Test impact: a single ATC edit changes several Tests without any action on those Tests, so a regression set can change between two runs of the same Test; run comparison then shows steps as Added, Removed or Not comparable. The audit row atc.updated lists the affected Tests (up to 3 titles in the Activity feed).
  • An archived ATC cannot be edited or duplicated (45025).

Data: business-data-context entity-atc, entity-run.

Cross-feature flow: notifications

  • Producers: Runs (finished or aborted, to the starter, unless the starter closed it from the browser), Bugs (assignment to the new assignee; status change to reporter and assignee, never the actor) and team chat mentions (one in-app notification per mentioned member). Nothing else notifies.
  • Preferences are applied when the event happens: in-app on stores a visible row; in-app off with email on stores an email-only row hidden from the inbox, bell and realtime; both off stores nothing. Mentions ignore preferences. Changing a preference later changes nothing already stored.
  • Inbox: the sidebar bell shows the unread count, a panel lists the last 90 days, rows arrive live; read one or "mark all read" (POST /api/v1/notifications/{id}/read, …/notifications/read-all). A mention row opens the chat dock on its message instead of a route.
  • Email: a daily digest at 08:00 UTC from production only (staging has no cron); its link opens the inbox through a query parameter (OpenInboxFromQuery). Email-only rows are digested once (emailed_at); visible rows are included while unread.
  • Preferences: Settings, Notifications, a grid of run and bug lifecycle times in-app and email (mentions locked); each cell saves on its own and a hung save is aborted after 15 seconds.
  • Test impact: a notification test needs two accounts (actor and recipient) because self-actions are suppressed; a digest test needs production cron or a call with CRON_SECRET.

Data: business-data-context flow-notifications, entity-notification.

Cross-feature flow: the active workspace

  • Every signed-in page resolves one active workspace from a cookie (falling back to the user's first workspace) and scopes the sidebar's projects, the ATC Library, Test Runs and Bug Reports counts, the role shown in the account menu, the notification count, the team chat and the settings navigation to it.
  • Project URLs carry only the project slug: /projects/{slug} is resolved inside the active workspace, so the same URL can mean a different project, or not found, after a switch.
  • Switching (POST /api/v1/me/active-workspace) refreshes the shell; role-dependent controls follow the new role; the chat panel is keyed by workspace and reloads.
  • The shell also shows a dismissible plan-limit banner to non-viewers near the project cap (80 percent warning, at-cap notice; dismissal lasts the browser session and comes back when the state worsens) and, when the active workspace was deleted under the user, a one-time "workspace deleted" notice.
  • Test impact: tenant isolation is tested by switching workspaces and by opening another workspace's ids directly; both must answer not found, never forbidden with data.

Entities in business-data-context with no user-facing feature: feature_flags (schema only), idempotency_keys, magic_link_tokens, stripe_webhook_events, notification_digest_log, workspace_deletions, rate_limit_hits, storage_cleanup_queue, run_submission_keys and workspace_grace_periods (internal bookkeeping). tests.automation_status has no write path.

API endpoint inventory (pointer)

Endpoint groups belong to business-api-context, whose map exists but was last generated on 2026-10-12 (before 17 further operations), so its group sections group-access, group-identity-tokens, group-workspace-lifecycle, group-invites, group-billing, group-structure, group-imports, group-atcs, group-test-design, group-runs, group-bugs, group-insights, group-notifications and group-platform do not list the newer routes yet. The current contract is /api/openapi: 119 operations in the QA repo's api/openapi-types.ts (synced from staging on 2026-11-17, was 102), across 120 route files. New operation families: team chat, saved views, milestone plans and archive, plan close and reopen, ATC bulk edit and restore, module restore, run compare, run submissions, step and bug evidence attachments, workspace bugs and runs lists, tracker settings, workspace Jira connection, billing details, invoices, payment method and retry, member removal, storage cleanup (cron). Each feature in this map names the endpoints its UI calls.

Global sidebar: Home, Activity, Projects (count badge), ATC Library, Test Runs, Bug Reports (each with a count badge and workspace-wide), Metrics (opens the current or first project's Metrics; disabled only with no project), Settings; a team chat toggle with unread badge; the notification bell; search; workspace switcher; account menu (Settings, Sign out). Project sub-nav: All ATCs, Tests, Test Runs, Bug Reports, Metrics, Traceability, Milestones, Test Plans, Settings. Settings nav: Account, Tokens, Workspaces, Notifications, Billing (admin, owner), Jira (admin, owner), Data export (owner); Members and Environments listed as coming soon.

Test accounts needed

Declared: one user per environment (LOCAL_USER_EMAIL, STAGING_USER_EMAIL, with their passwords). Needed for the journeys above: one account per role (viewer, member, admin, owner) in a shared workspace, plus a second member for notification, assignment and mention tests, plus a disposable owner for deletion, removal and billing tests. Whether the QA repo's member-removal tests create such accounts through the API was not reviewed.

Smoke scope suggestion

Sign in, open Home, open a project workbench, open a Test, start and abort a run on a seeded environment, open Bug Reports. Each step uses only member rights and no external dependency. Add: send and read one chat message, open the ATC Library.

Discovery gaps

  • No browser session was run for this map (code, maps and read-only MCPs only): every journey is traced from code at origin/staging 4ccd8ed, and UI timing, layout and live-update behaviour are unverified.
  • The API map (business-api-context) exists but dates from 2026-10-12, so it lacks roughly 17 newer operations and the endpoint pointers here cite openapi-types.ts instead of section ids.
  • Signed-out behaviour of /runs and /bugs: both are outside PROTECTED_PREFIXES in middleware.ts and their pages contain no redirect; what an unauthenticated visitor sees was not verified.
  • Viewers can still open atcs/new and tests/new and the ATC editor's save has no role check of its own; the exact message a viewer gets on save was not verified.
  • Every project's explorer and Tests list show all Tests of the workspace, including Tests whose ATCs are in other projects; intended (Tests are workspace-scoped) or a display bug is not confirmed.
  • The browser ATC editor saves last-write-wins by design (ifMatch: null); whether the product owner accepts silent overwrites between two people in the browser was not confirmed.
  • Run start with an archived ATC in the chain: the Test view marks it, but whether the start refuses or copies it was not verified (also in the data map gaps).
  • The message shown when the project limit refuses a new project is covered by PlanLimitModal, but the exact copy for an owner versus a member was not read.
  • Whether a viewer can create or apply a saved view (API write needs atc:write) was not verified.
  • Whether the workspace data export includes chat messages, saved views, attachments, the Jira connection or billing records was not verified; lib/workspace-export lists projects, modules, stories, criteria, ATCs, Tests, runs, bugs, activity and memberships.
  • No code sends a bug to Jira although bugs.sync_state, the project settings and the connection exist; whether this is deliberate staging of the feature is a product question.
  • No evidence attachment (run step or bug) and no milestone with an attached plan exists in the shared database, so those features are traced from code only.
  • Failed-renewal communication: no Bunkai email for a failed renewal or a member removal was found; the banner is the only announcement. Stripe-side emails were not checked.
  • Password reset, profile edit and member role change: no route or form found. Not verified whether Supabase's hosted flows cover any of them.
  • Which role STAGING_USER_EMAIL holds, and in which workspace, was not verified (secret values are not read).
  • GitHub and Google OAuth provider configuration per environment, Stripe test mode on staging, Resend delivery on staging and Jira Cloud access for a test workspace: not verified.
  • Domain and infra maps were refreshed on 2026-11-17 (commit 2ae9e54); this map did not re-check them for contradictions beyond the ATC name ("Acceptance Test Case").
  • /about is in Spanish while the app UI is English; the target audience of each public page was not confirmed.
  • Usage numbers come from a database shared by local, staging and production and filled mostly by automated tests; they show what is exercised, not customer behaviour. The workspace_jira_connections table is not readable by the QA role, so the number of connected workspaces is unknown.
  • The data map (2026-11-17) is the source for database counts and rules cited here as "data map"; any divergence found later belongs in its own gaps.
  • No legacy persona, journey or functional-spec files exist (.context/PRD/, .context/SRS/, .context/business/ are absent), so nothing was migrated.
